media.title: Ernst Lubitsch with his secretary, Hollywood, 1930 — photograph by Erich Salomon
media.description: Ernst Lubitsch at his desk in Hollywood, taking papers from his secretary, photographed by Erich Salomon in 1930. Lubitsch was one of the founders of the European Film Fund in 1938.
media.altText: Black-and-white photograph of Ernst Lubitsch, cigar in mouth, seated at a desk and taking a stack of papers from a standing woman.
media.publicCaption: Ernst Lubitsch in Hollywood, 1930, photographed by Erich Salomon. Lubitsch was among the founders of the European Film Fund.
media.publicCreditLine: Erich Salomon, 1930; Berlinische Galerie; via Wikimedia Commons.
media.rightsNote: Public domain. Erich Salomon died in 1944, so the European term of life and seventy years ran out at the end of 2014. In the United States the photograph is free either way: first published in 1930, its restored term ran to the end of 2025; if it stayed unpublished, the term of life and seventy years ran out with the European one.

timelineEvents.title: European Film Fund established
timelineEvents.label: 1938 · European Film Fund
timelineEvents.shortDescription: The European Film Fund was established in 1938 to aid refugees from the European film community; a later donor list documents Kaper’s involvement.
timelineEvents.longDescription: The European Film Fund was established in 1938 by Paul Kohner, Ernst Lubitsch and Carl Laemmle to aid refugees arriving from Europe. Kaper’s involvement is documented by a surviving donor list covering 1 May 1941–30 April 1942, which records “Kaper, Bronislaw” and a contribution of $120. The list does not establish when he first became involved.
